<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 54159fd742e5a79fc10ac41854dba3395e1a1ffe` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2cd17fe7e2f0cbb489a68d560f2442af3441fcf3` — the merge of head `5697a4d225f3130e5b18f05d7a20489a4101bbe7` into base `54159fd742e5a79fc10ac41854dba3395e1a1ffe`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2cd17fe7e2f0cbb489a68d560f2442af3441fcf3 && git checkout 2cd17fe7e2f0cbb489a68d560f2442af3441fcf3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 54159fd742e5a79fc10ac41854dba3395e1a1ffe 5697a4d225f3130e5b18f05d7a20489a4101bbe7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 54159fd742e5a79fc10ac41854dba3395e1a1ffe && git merge --no-ff 5697a4d225f3130e5b18f05d7a20489a4101bbe7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 54159fd742e5a79fc10ac41854dba3395e1a1ffe
```

</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than

> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 54159fd742e5a79fc10ac41854dba3395e1a1ffe` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5697a4d225f3130e5b18f05d7a20489a4101bbe7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages-manifest-patch-readonly.test.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-writability.ts (`isWritablePackage`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (`updatePackage`, the class constructor), packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts (`handlePackages`, `resolveService`, the `error` deps), packages/runtime/src/error-envelope.ts (`buildApiError`), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`registerApp`), packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`installPackage`), docs/adr/0070-package-first-authoring.md (D2), docs/adr/0131-total-organization-ownership-no-null-organization-id.md (D6), scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, .github/workflows/pr-automation.yml (the `Check Changeset` job, WHICH LEVEL), packages/runtime/vitest.config.ts + vitest.repo-tests.json, packages/runtime/tsconfig.test.json, the swept pins (packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/error-passthrough.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages-readonly-gate.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages-install-overwrite-readonly.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-body-after-anonymous-floor.hono.integration.test.ts, packages/client/src/packages-write-envelope.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.package-persist-failure.test.ts, docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/api-backend.json), the precedent changeset at `62f959dd6` (.changeset/24030-install-overwrite-readonly-package.md), and objectui `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PackagesPage.tsx` at the `.objectui-sha` pin `12dc7b47c`. The prose face .changeset/24705-patch-manifest-readonly-package.md is judged in ②.

### ① Derived judgments

Net diff against `main` at `54159fd74` (merge base `1c1144fcd`, three commits on the branch): +256 / −0 over three files. `packages.ts` gains exactly one call plus its comment at the `PATCH /packages/:id` arm, and nothing else in the file moves.

**Check-runs on the head (the gate verdicts).** 39 runs, latest per name: 29 `success`, 0 failed, 6 `skipped` (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, the Dogfood matrix shard, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance), and **4 still `in_progress`: Test Core (1/6), (2/6), (3/6), (4/6)**. Those four are NOT MEASURED by this record; `Test Core (5/6)` and `(6/6)` are `success`. Also `success`: `Check Changeset` (the job that runs both `check-adr-0087-registration` and `check-changeset-no-major`), every `Lint ·` family, every `Type Check ·` family, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and the three claim guards. The judgments below are made on the diff.

1. **The accept-set change the diff publishes — RIGHT.**
   - `isWritablePackage` answers `false` for an id in `engine.manifests` (booted by `registerApp`, as code or marketplace) and for a registry row whose manifest `scope` is `system` / `cloud`.
   - For such a package, `PATCH /api/v1/packages/:id` moves from `200` with the manifest edited (and, with a `package` service composed, `sys_packages` re-persisted by `protocol.updatePackage`) to `422` `WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED`, with nothing written.
   - Governing text holds. ADR-0070 D2 makes exactly those two kinds read-only and names "a single predicate reused by all surfaces". `package-writability.ts` is that predicate, and the diff calls it through the domain's existing `requireWritablePackage`, re-deriving nothing.
   - Every other state-changing arm on the domain already asks it, read at the head: `:1410` install-overwrite, `:1602` disable, `:1629` publish, `:2114` revert, `:2318` delete. So the door now gives the answer its siblings give, and the arm's new comment names those five siblings correctly.

2. **Position of the gate (manage, then walled, then writable, before the body) — RIGHT.**
   - The PATCH arm now reads `requireManageMetadata` → `refuseWalledCatalogPackageWrite` → `requireWritablePackage` → body.
   - Disable (`:1596-1602`) and delete (`:2306-2318`, with its `keepData` arity read between walled and writable) use that order. Publish and install-overwrite place the gate after their own earlier refusals (the `409`), and revert after the protocol's stored-row answer, each for a reason its comment states. So the PR body's "manage, walled, writable" claim is accurate for this arm and its nearest siblings.
   - The changeset discloses the consequence correctly: for a read-only id, a body the arm would itself refuse `400` (`{}`, a non-SemVer `version`) answers `422`, because the refusal precedes the body read. That is the shape the card and the triage asked for ("gate the whole arm before the body is read").

3. **An unknown id keeps the arm's own `404` on both limbs — RIGHT.**
   - `isWritablePackage` returns `true` for a non-empty id with no `manifests` entry and no registry row (`package-writability.ts:73-82`), so the gate falls through.
   - The fallback limb's `registry.updatePackageManifest` answers `undefined` → `404`. The protocol limb's `updatePackage` throws `statusCode: 404` (the `updatePackage` body in `protocol.ts`), which `errorFromThrown` carries.
   - The predicate's empty-id branch (`!packageId` → not writable) is unreachable here. `parts = path.replace(/^\/+/, '').split('/').filter(Boolean)` (`packages.ts:1078`), and the arm requires `parts.length === 1`, so `id` is a non-empty decoded segment. The gate is not an existence oracle, exactly as its doc block demands.

4. **Wire envelope — RIGHT.**
   - `deps.error(message, 422, { code, packageId, docs })` → `buildApiError` promotes `details.code` to `error.code`, keeps `packageId` and `docs` under `error.details`, and sets `error.httpStatus: 422` (`error-envelope.ts`, `splitSemanticCode` + `buildApiError`).
   - The new pins assert exactly that shape, plus `details.docs === 'docs/adr/0070-package-first-authoring.md'`.
   - With verb `edit`, the refusal reads "Cannot edit package 'ID': it is read-only (provided by code or an installed app). Packages the deployment ships are managed by the deployment, not over this API — edit a package you own, or customise … (ADR-0131 D6)".
   - The D6 remedy clause is the shared `CUSTOMISE_BESIDE_REMEDY`, and it matches ADR-0131 D6's managed-mode text ("no door edits a managed definition … what the customer changes lives beside the managed item").

5. **No other public surface moves — RIGHT.**
   - `requireWritablePackage` is module-private.
   - No export, spec key, stored shape or REST route-ledger row changes. The PATCH door is dispatcher-only and absent from `packages/rest/src/rest-route-ledger.ts`, as `api-backend.json:1053` records.
   - The `writable` verdict the list and detail doors serve is untouched.
   - `Type Check · *` and `TypeScript Type Check` are `success`.

6. **The pins — RIGHT in construction; the CI verdict is pending.**
   - `packages-manifest-patch-readonly.test.ts` is under `src/**/*.test.ts` and not in `vitest.repo-tests.json`, so it is in the `local` project (`vitest.config.ts:234-236`) that `Test Core` shards. It is in the `tsconfig.test.json` program (`include` reaches `src`), and `TypeScript Type Check` is green on it.
   - Its harness has the same shape as the ACCEPTed precedent pin `packages-install-overwrite-readonly.test.ts`:
     - the same real `ObjectQL`;
     - `registerApp(manifest, undefined, 'marketplace')`, matching `registerApp(registeredBody, scope?, source = 'code')` at `engine.ts:8369`;
     - `registry.installPackage(manifest, 'authored')`, matching `(manifest, source, settings?, scope?)` at `registry.ts:5873`;
     - `new ObjectStackProtocolImplementation(engine, servicesGetter)` with a thunk returning the services map, matching the constructor `(engine, getServicesRegistry?, environmentId?, authoringChannel?)` at `protocol.ts:7062`;
     - the same kernel double, and `resolveService` tolerates a `getService` that answers `null`.
   - 32 refusal rows (4 read-only kinds × 4 bodies × 2 limbs) read the observables, not the status alone: the row snapshot by value, `updatePackageManifest` never called, `protocol.updatePackage` never called, and the `package` service's `publish` never called.
   - 6 CONTROL rows: a writable edit answers `200` and the row and `sys_packages` spies really move; a writable `{}` still answers `400`; an unknown id still answers `404`, with `updatePackageManifest` called once.
   - The dev reports 32 failed / 6 passed at base and after a trap-armed ablation of the one call, and 38 passed at the head. This record does not re-run them. The four `Test Core` shards that would carry this file's CI verdict are `in_progress`, so that verdict is NOT MEASURED here.

7. **Full-repo pin sweep, re-read on the head tree — RIGHT.** No existing test asserts a `200` PATCH of a read-only id:
   - `http-dispatcher.test.ts`'s PATCH cases run over `{ registry: mockRegistry }` with no `manifests` and no `getPackage`, so the package is writable;
   - `error-passthrough.test.ts:141` uses a double;
   - `packages-write-envelope.test.ts` (client) only PATCHes `/enable` and `/disable`, and so does `packages-readonly-gate.test.ts`;
   - `dispatcher-body-after-anonymous-floor.hono.integration.test.ts` uses the unknown `pkg_x`;
   - `protocol.package-persist-failure.test.ts` calls `impl.updatePackage` directly, under the gate;
   - `api-backend.json:1049` PATCHes a package the item installs with `scope: 'project'`.

   The other `WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED` hits are the authoring path's, and they are untouched.

8. **Serial with PR #24703 — RIGHT as stated.** The PATCH arm on base `main` `54159fd74` carries neither the gate nor a `dependencies` hunk, so #24703 has not landed, and this PR lands first as triage `6280778865` ordered. Because the gate precedes the body read, the `{ dependencies: {} }` rows hold on either tree.

9. **Governance — RIGHT.**
   - No governed path is in the file list. `record-recognisers --template --paths` on the three paths decides no face on paths alone and defers to the changeset's `Clause-②` arm → narrowing → `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, which is this record.
   - `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is `success`.
   - 256 lines, under the human-merge threshold.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/runtime': minor` — RIGHT.
- The act is a BREAKING narrowing of a published REST door's accept set. AGENTS.md Post-Task item 3 makes `(narrowing)` BREAKING, so the ordinary `patch` for a bug fix does not describe it.
- During the launch window `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` refuses `major`, and breaking-ness is carried by the **BREAKING** banner plus the ADR-0087 disposition, not by the level (the script's header, and the `Check Changeset` step's WHICH LEVEL prose, `pr-automation.yml:754-775`). So `minor` is the level the convention gives. The precedent changeset at `62f959dd6` (the install-overwrite sibling, ACCEPTed) graded the same act `minor` in the same form.
- The changeset carries the `fix(runtime)!:` title, the **BREAKING** banner, and FROM / TO / Unchanged / "the fix for an integrator", which is the migration text item 3 requires of a breaking changeset.
- It carries exactly one ADR-0087 marker (an HTML comment) reading `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, a category the gate lists (`check-adr-0087-registration.mjs:147,539`). Its refusal condition, a code-rewrite prescription in the body, is not met: the integrator line is the remedy ADR-0131 D6 names, not a rewrite.
- No other package's code changes, so no second changeset is owed; `packages/client` forwards the envelope unchanged.
- `Check Changeset`, the job that runs both gates on this PR, is `success` on the head.

`Clause-②:` line — RIGHT. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is on both the PR body and the changeset: no key is added to any published payload (`no`), and the door's accept set shrinks (`(narrowing)`, the one arm allowed with `no`). The two spellings agree, which is what `check-adr-0087-registration` reads. The claim comment `6280929612` carries a bare `Clause-②: no`. The dev named that in the report rather than choosing silently, and the arm belongs on the PR body and the changeset, where it is.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: none declared. The dev's `deviations` (5), its `out_of_scope_findings` (1) and the PR's Acceptance notes (3) are each answered below.

1. **`origin/main` was not merged before opening** — answered, accepted. Main gained six commits since `1c1144fcd`, and the base's `packages.ts` PATCH arm, `package-writability.ts`, `protocol.updatePackage` and the registry's package methods are as the branch read them. CI measured the merge ref `2cd17fe7e`, and the queue merges onto `main` anyway.
2. **Bare `Clause-②: no` on the claim comment vs `no (narrowing)` on the PR body and changeset** — answered in ②: the spellings the gate reads carry the arm, and they are right.
3. **The `--ran` record line was rewritten after the `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` re-run on a fully built tree** — answered, no bearing. It is local bookkeeping, and the head's check-runs are the gate verdicts here.
4. **Model-free commit trailers** — answered, accepted. The repo's pre-push hook refuses a model identifier, and AGENTS.md outranks the harness reminder.
5. **Pins widened beyond the dispatch (four kinds × four bodies × two limbs)** — answered, accepted. It is a strict superset with the same assertions, and the cloud-scoped and marketplace kinds are the predicate's own branches.
6. **The out-of-scope finding (carrier: none, noted not filed): objectui's Packages detail sheet decides its action buttons from `manifest.scope` (`isKernel`), while its Scope badge reads the served `writable` verdict.**
   - Verified at the pin `12dc7b47c`: `isKernel = pkg.manifest.scope === 'system' || pkg.manifest.scope === 'cloud'` (`PackagesPage.tsx:491`), and Edit (`setEditOpen`), Publish and the rest sit in the `!isKernel` arm (`:874-890`).
   - So a code-booted or marketplace package whose scope is `project` or absent is offered Edit, Disable, Publish, Revert and Delete, and each answers `422` (Edit only since this PR; the other four already).
   - Answered: not a blocker for this PR. The server's refusal is the contract, and the dialog renders the envelope's message.
   - ESCALATED to the owning seat as a filing recommendation: a sibling-repo (`objectui`) card, `area:studio`, "detail-sheet action buttons should read the served `writable` verdict (objectui#12723 did this for the badge)". The dev's dedupe words stand.
7. **`requireWritablePackage`'s doc block in `packages.ts` lists its doors (#7560 lifecycle, #22113 publish/revert) and names neither this door nor install-overwrite** — answered, accepted. It is an in-file comment on a private function, already stale from `62f959dd6`. The arm's own comment names the door, and no gate reads the list. Tidy it the next time that block is touched.
8. **`packages/client`'s `packages.update` JSDoc does not mention the refusal** — answered, accepted. The client's behaviour is unchanged (it forwards the envelope), and no changeset is owed on it.
9. **Carried from the card, still NOT measured: what a code package's stored `sys_packages` row (written by an earlier edit) does on the next boot** — ESCALATED back to card #24705 as an open measurement outside this PR's scope. This PR stops new edits and touches no stored row. The card's own Persistence line already marks it NOT measured, and it stays there for the lane.
10. **Docs Drift Check advisory (`content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` via `handlePackagesRequest`)** — answered, no action. That page states caller-permission rules; this change adds a package-property refusal after the permission gate and moves no permission rule.
